City of Surrey · Council term 2022–2026

How each Councillor voted

Independent summary, not affiliated with the City of Surrey. Every Council vote from November 2022 to June 2026, rebuilt from the City of Surrey's official meeting minutes (204 sets, the most recent posted). Surrey doesn't publish a voting table, so each vote was read from the minutes, which name anyone who opposed. Surrey's Council handles far more items than the others, most of them land-use applications, so this page has thousands of votes. Routine motions such as adopting the agenda or adjourning are left out.

Summary

Key findings

  • Most votes are unanimous, but the divisions are sharp and consistent. 92% of votes (7,755 of 8,457) had no one opposed. The 702 split votes follow the same lines again and again.
  • A five-member majority: Mayor Brenda Locke with Harry Bains, Gordon Hepner, Pardeep Kooner and Rob Stutt. They agree on 84–95% of split votes. Bains, Kooner and Stutt are on the winning side 91–97% of the time, and Locke 85%.
  • Linda Annis is the most frequent dissenter (486 “no” votes) and is on the losing side of 71% of split votes. Her closest ally is Mike Bose (78% agreement). The two voted together against increases to building, business licence, electrical, fire service, animal and other City fees, 139 votes in all.
  • Mandeep Nagra and Doug Elford form a second minority pair (77% agreement). Annis, Bose, Elford and Nagra opposed the 2024–2028 and later financial plans and tax levies, which passed 5–4.
  • Cannabis stores cut across the usual lines. Mayor Locke, Hepner, Nagra and Stutt voted against each cannabis retail rezoning, and the stores were approved 5–4 by the other five members.
  • A proposal to expand Council from eight to ten councillors was defeated 5–4 in May 2025. The majority bloc voted it down; Annis, Bose, Elford and Nagra supported it.
  • Attendance varies widely. Nagra missed 24 meetings and Annis 14; Rob Stutt missed almost none. Absent members aren't counted in the “against” rates.

Who votes with whom

Categories

How each member votes, by category

Categories are assigned from keywords in each motion's title and text, since Surrey's minutes don't tag topics. Each cell shows "no" votes out of votes cast in that category. Darker cells mean a higher share of "no" votes. A "no" is a vote against one specific motion, which is often an amendment, a referral or a motion to reject something, so these counts don't show whether a member supports or opposes the topic itself. Open the votes to see what each motion said. A vote can belong to more than one category: a rezoning for a six-storey rental building counts under both Housing & density and Development. Click a category name to see its votes in the log below.

Method

How to read this

Source. The City of Surrey's Council meeting archive: 204 sets of Regular Council – Land Use, Regular Council – Public Hearing, Council-in-Committee, Finance Committee, Special and Inaugural minutes from 7 November 2022 to 15 June 2026 (the latest posted), retrieved 29 September 2026. Each vote links to its minutes and the meeting video.

How votes were counted. Surrey records each result as “Carried” or “Defeated” with a resolution number, followed by the names of anyone opposed. Members named as opposed are counted against; everyone else present is counted for. Attendance comes from each meeting's present and absent lists, adjusted when a member declared a conflict of interest and left, or joined late.

“Against” means against that motion. Referrals, amendments and motions to reject something are separate votes, and a “no” on them can mean support for the underlying item. Expand any row to read the motion.

Limits. When a member stepped out briefly and returned, the minutes don't say which votes they missed, so they're counted as present. Each reading of a bylaw is its own vote, so a contested bylaw can appear three or four times. Two Finance Committee documents have no attendance list, so all members are assumed present for those. Motion text is shortened on this page; the linked minutes are the official record.

Categories. Each vote is sorted by keywords in its title and motion text. A vote can sit in several categories, and some placements are judgment calls.

Privacy. Names of residents who spoke at meetings are removed from the motion text here.

How this page was made. The votes were read from the official records by software and checked against samples of the originals. The summaries and topic categories were written and assigned with AI assistance, and they can contain mistakes. Where a summary and the vote log differ, the vote log and the linked official records are correct.
